- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.1), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to cap the peak; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to reflect market cooling.
- If model shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops) with negative sentiment, it often fails to capture mean reversion; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias in 5–7 day horizon to reflect reversal.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.05), model tends to underestimate upward momentum; increase forecast by 0.3–0.8% for next 7–14 days to capture sentiment-driven rally.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply 0.5–1.0% upward bias for first 3 days if sentiment > -0.1.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 5–7 days if sentiment > 0.1.
